correctness.rationale: The Ren–Chen theorem gives only three specified two-distinct-prime families plus 40. For e=v2(N), all satisfy N<2^(3e+2); for odd g, LTE gives v2(U_l(g))=0 for odd l and v2(g+1)+v2(l)−1 for even l. Since a<g≤9, e≤5+log2(l), whence 3^(l−1)≤N<2^17·l³ and monotonicity bounds 3≤l≤19 and 1≤e≤9. This converts infinite families into 31 explicitly enumerated prime-admissible candidates. An independently written exact arithmetic sieve of all 31 candidates against g=3,5,7,9 and l=3..19 produced only 40 as 1111 base3; sigma(40)=90=80+10, with proper d=10 and omega=2.
